text:
Jess: Heads-up — customer 'P-12' is seeing periodic healthcheck failures when we rotate outbound SNAT from the edge. They only whitelisted a single IP on their firewall and our NAT pool cycles across ~8 IPs. Can we suggest a clean mitigation?

Tim: Ouuch. Do we know if it's the healthcheck flow specifically failing (SYN or app-level)?

Jess: Logs show TCP RST on follow-up connections. Initial SYN succeeds but subsequent checks hit different source IPs and their FW blocks them. So the LB reports unhealthy after 2 failures.

Riya: Got it. Classic source-ip rotation + stateful firewall. Need two quick asks: 1) can customer expand allowlist to the whole NAT CIDR? 2) can we advise them to accept sourceport range used by ephemeral ports?

Jess: They asked for minimal blast radius — won't open /24. Proposed a soak test where we pin healthcheck traffic to one IP for 24h and see if ops team will accept adding that single IP.

Tim: Two notes: (a) pinning is possible via sticky SNAT allocation for a short period but relies on conntrack/timeouts; (b) if they use an outbound proxy that terminates TLS, hairpinning and preserve-source-port flags matter.

Riya: Also check ephemeral port exhaustion risk — if their firewall does source port mapping rules, mixing different source ports can look like new flows and get blocked. Suggest they allow ephemeral 32768-61000 or we keep a small port pool.

Jess: Proposed message to CS: "We can run a 24h pinned-SNAT soak and provide the single IP. If that works, please add that IP to your firewall and we'll schedule a controlled rotation window."

Alex (cs): I'll coordinate with the customer. Quick Q: what exact IP range should we ask them to open if they can't do single-IP?

Riya: Give them the provider NAT CIDR used for that edge: 198.51.100.128/26 (example allocation) — that's 64 IPs. Recommend opening TCP 443 and any healthcheck-specific port. Also include DNS egress for healthchecks that resolve service names.

Tim: For customers that refuse CIDR-level allowlisting, we usually recommend one of the following: (1) use a TLS-terminating proxy inside their network + mutual TLS with our service, (2) route healthchecks via a dedicated static-egress appliance (Dedicated customers), or (3) accept SNI-based allowlist on their firewall (if vendor supports SNI-based rules).

Jess: Adding practical config snippet we sent to a customer earlier for sticky SNAT testing:

```
# curl-based healthcheck example (use --resolve to force host to IP)
curl -v --resolve my-service.example:443:203.0.113.45 \
  https://my-service.example/healthz -H 'Host: my-service.example' \
  --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 8
```

Jess: Also asked infra to open an internal ticket to track the soak test and IP allocation.

InfraBot: Ticket EDGE-EGRESS-945 created and assigned to @tim (details: pinned SNAT allocation request, 24h soak, customer P-12).

Tim: I'll allocate one sticky IP for 24hrs and post it here once live. Meanwhile Alex, please get their firewall contact and confirm maintenance window.

Alex (cs): On it. Will report back once they confirm. :thumbsup:
